questions.question: Which entity correctly escapes the less-than sign (<) in HTML?
questions.explanation: < represents the reserved less-than character (<) in HTML.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the   entity?
options: It creates a non-breaking space that prevents automatic line wrapping
It formats text as monospace code
It applies a neon shadow to text
questions.explanation: inserts a non-breaking space, ensuring that connected words stay together on the same line.

questions.question: Every HTML character entity must begin with which character and end with which character?
questions.hint: Ampersand at start, semicolon at end.
questions.explanation: Entities always start with an ampersand (&) and conclude with a semicolon (;).

questions.question: Which entity renders the copyright symbol (©)?
Why must the ampersand (&) be written as & in valid HTML body text?
options: Because & is the reserved character used by the browser to initiate entities
Because & is reserved for CSS variables
Because & slows down TCP packet delivery
Because & causes memory leaks in JavaScript
questions.hint: The ampersand signals the start of an entity.
questions.explanation: Because '&' triggers entity parsing in HTML engines, displaying a literal ampersand requires &.
